summary: P0 Collector API-Key Authentication: fully validated. Ran the two targeted pytest suites in-process (test_collector_api_key_auth.py = 33 passed, test_p0sec_rbac_fail_closed.py = 21 passed) and an independent adversarial regression against the live preview backend URL (test_collector_api_key_adversarial_regression.py = 18 passed). 72/72 tests pass. Fail-closed matrix, credential-non-blending, tenant binding, scope gating, SHA-256-only storage, no plaintext path, usage telemetry, JWT admin regression, and anonymous P0-SEC regression (including spoofed principal headers) are all correct.

minor.issue: POST /api/xdr/ingest/telemetry with valid enroll-scoped key and body {envelopes:[{tenant_id:<other>, source:'x', events:[]}]} returns 422 body-validation, not 403. Not a security bypass (auth gate passed, downstream body validation caught the mismatch), but a defence-in-depth ergonomic gap: cross-tenant envelope should ideally be a distinct 403 tenant-isolation denial rather than shape validation. Report only, out of scope for this P0.

critical_code_review_comments: Machine-auth path in xdr_rbac.authenticate_api_key uses hashlib.sha256 lookup + hmac.compare_digest with no plaintext fallback — verified by source-guard test and by grep of the function body.
require_permission correctly refuses ambiguous-credentials when both HTTPBearer creds and X-XDR-API-Key are present (an invalid JWT never falls through to key auth).

expires_at=null intentionally means never-expires; confirmed via test_expires_at_null_is_accepted_as_never_expires. Malformed expiry strings are NOT treated as never-expiring (api-key-expiry-malformed 403).
HTTP header names are case-insensitive at Starlette/FastAPI layer; lowercase/mixed-case X-XDR-API-Key work against the live URL, as expected. No case-sensitivity bypass exists.

Pre-existing failures deferred by main agent and reconfirmed as unchanged: tests/test_xdr_api_keys.py, tests/test_xdr_rbac_enforcement.py, tests/test_p0_f4_endpoint_process_tree.py — all traceable to legacy X-Tenant-Id/X-Principal-Id header seeding which P0-SEC intentionally stopped honouring. NOT caused by this change.
